prompt.context: Bill's Chips is a multinational producer of snacks. Their largest snack by total sales volume is potato chips. Currently, they are losing market share to their competitors in certain regions of the world. They are attempting to determine which market is the best to enter with a goal to maximize profitability in year 3. They have hired you to help with their assessment. Additional background: Bill's Chips is headquartered in Durham, NC and has an extremely established brand with high customer loyalty. The industry is highly competitive and consumers' largest driver of choice is taste preference. They sell chips globally across all segments. Customers are grocery stores who resell to consumers. There is no specific profitability margin they are seeking — they are aiming to maximize profit over 3 years.
prompt.question: Which market should Bill's Chips enter to maximize profitability by year 3?

clarifying_info.q: Is there a minimum profitability threshold they need to hit?
clarifying_info.a: No specific margin target — they are aiming to maximize profit over 3 years.

clarifying_info.q: Are the market size figures in units or dollars?
clarifying_info.a: These are units sold (figures in millions of dollars — great candidates will clarify currency).

clarifying_info.q: Do they already have manufacturing or distribution in any of these markets?
clarifying_info.a: No additional information is provided; assume they would be entering fresh.

exhibits.title: Market Overview by Region
exhibits.shows: A table of four candidate markets — Brazil, Western Canada, Western Europe, and Australia — each with market size, current penetration rate, and annual growth rate.

exhibits.title: Chip Flavor Pricing and Costs
exhibits.shows: A table of three chip flavors available for the European market — Beer Battered Cod, Tuscan Wine, and Lime Kiwi — with sales price, manufacturing cost, and ingredient cost per bag.

framework: MARKET: Assess competition (fragmented vs. few large players, anticipated penetration), market size (population and value), and growth trajectory (expand vs. contract over 5 years)
PROFITABILITY — Revenue: Understand market rate for chips, whether Bill's Chips is priced above/below market, bag sizes and SKU options
PROFITABILITY — Cost: Break down fixed costs (factories, fixed contracts) vs. variable costs (potatoes, ingredients, employee wages)
EXTERNAL FACTORS: Geopolitical risks and tariffs between countries, commodity price volatility from supply chain or scarcity, labor strikes in a highly unionized industry
Drive analysis toward calculating total addressable market size after 3-year growth, then overlay profitability per unit to rank markets

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, calculate the addressable market size for each region at Year 3 and identify the most attractive market by volume.
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute Year 0 penetrated units (market size × penetration), then compound at the annual growth rate for 3 years. Australia should quickly be dismissed as the smallest market with the lowest penetration and growth. The candidate should identify Western Europe as the largest market at Year 3. Strong candidates use compound-growth shortcuts (multiply by the compounding factor) rather than stepping through each year. Great candidates comment on why certain markets are larger or growing faster (e.g., Brazil's emerging middle class).

math.setup: Year 0 penetrated units = Market Size × Current Penetration. Compound for 3 years at annual growth rate.
math.answer: Western Europe is the largest market at Year 3 with ~8.6–8.7M units, followed by Western Canada ~7.8–8.0M, then Brazil ~5.1M. Australia is negligible and should be dismissed.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, calculate profit per bag for each flavor and determine the most profitable chip to sell in Western Europe.
questions.guidance: Candidate should subtract manufacturing cost and ingredient cost from sales price to get profit per bag, then rank the three flavors. Strong candidates also compute profit margin percentages. The answer is Lime Kiwi with $2.00 profit per bag and an ~80% margin, which is far superior to Beer Battered Cod ($1.50 / ~50% margin) and Tuscan Wine ($1.25 / ~42% margin). Second-level insight: discuss why input cost differs (distribution of raw materials, packaging, specialty flavors, potatoes).

math.setup: Profit per bag = Sales Price − Manufacturing Cost − Ingredient Cost
math.answer: Lime Kiwi is the most profitable flavor at $2.00 profit per bag and an 80% margin, despite the lowest sale price.

questions.prompt: Calculate total 3-year profit for Bill's Chips entering Western Europe with Lime Kiwi chips.
questions.guidance: Multiply the Year 3 market volume by profit per bag to get Year 3 annual profit. Strong candidates also sum all three years to get total 3-year profit (~$49–51M). Candidate should confirm currency (millions of dollars).

math.setup: Annual profit = Year N volume × $2.00 profit per bag (Lime Kiwi). Sum Year 1 + Year 2 + Year 3 for total.
math.answer: Year 3 annual profit ≈ $17.2–17.4M; total 3-year cumulative profit ≈ $49–51M.

brainstorming.prompt: Bill's Chips is concerned about rising costs. What can they do to minimize and/or stabilize costs? (Brainstorm should be structured — e.g., by value chain or fixed vs. variable.)

categories.name: Internal
ideas: Reallocate personnel to optimize performance and reduce headcount costs
Optimize manufacturing process — identify overlap or unnecessary steps to cut waste
Increase efficiency and pass-rate of chip quality inspections to reduce rework and spoilage

categories.name: External / Supply Chain
ideas: Minimize supply chain distance by sourcing from local farmers in or near the target market
Secure long-term fixed-price contracts for raw materials (potatoes, flavoring ingredients, packaging) to hedge against commodity volatility
Minimize storage space required for raw materials to reduce warehousing costs

categories.name: Bonus: Manufacturing Footprint
ideas: Evaluate whether to set up a new manufacturing facility in Western Europe vs. using existing global logistics — cost savings from proximity need to be weighed against capex and ramp-up time

recommendation: Bill's Chips should enter the Western European market with the Lime Kiwi flavor chip.

This market delivers the largest Year 3 volume (~8.6–8.7M units), and Lime Kiwi's $2.00 profit per bag (80% margin) maximizes profitability — generating approximately $17.2M in Year 3 and ~$49–51M cumulatively over 3 years.
risks: Changing consumer taste preferences in Western Europe may reduce demand for Lime Kiwi flavor
Competitive pressure could force price reductions, compressing the $2.00 per bag margin
Commodity price increases (kiwi, lime, specialty ingredients) could erode the currently low input cost advantage
next_steps: Begin production prototyping of Lime Kiwi chips and run consumer taste tests in the Western European market to validate demand
Perform deeper market research to confirm growth projections and competitive dynamics in Western Europe
Evaluate supply chain and manufacturing options (local vs. centralized production) to lock in cost structure before entry
